gloss: immediately before; just before; right before

definitions.gloss: immediately before; just before; right before
definitions.explanation: At the very last moment before something happens. Emphasizes how close in time something is to a reference event.

examples.japanese: {出発|しゅっぱつ}{直前|ちょくぜん}に{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た。
examples.english: A phone call came right before departure.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{直前|ちょくぜん}に{体調|たいちょう}を{崩|くず}した。
examples.english: I fell ill just before the exam.

examples.japanese: {締|し}め{切|き}りの{直前|ちょくぜん}になって、やっと{資料|しりょう}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: The materials finally arrived just before the deadline.

notes:
Composed of {直|ちょく} (direct, immediately) and {前|ぜん} (before) + に (adverbial particle). Often used without に when modifying a noun directly: {直前|ちょくぜん}の{準備|じゅんび} (last-minute preparations). The の form functions as a pre-noun modifier.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {出発|しゅっぱつ}{直前|ちょくぜん}に: right before departure
- {締|し}め{切|き}り{直前|ちょくぜん}に: just before the deadline
- {直前|ちょくぜん}になって: at the last moment
- {直前|ちょくぜん}まで: until the very last moment

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {寸前|すんぜん}に: on the verge of — emphasizes extreme closeness, often to danger or crisis
- {直後|ちょくご}に: immediately after — the temporal opposite
- ぎりぎりに: at the last possible moment — more colloquial, emphasizes barely making it
